postTypes.name: Consensus guides
postTypes.how: "Best X in London" pages, ranked by how many independent sources name each place. Built with the consensus-guide skill. Each has a topic file, a sources file and a fact-check script.

postTypes.name: Walking routes
postTypes.how: Numbered stops in walking order, with a map, a Google Maps link and what is open on which day. Built with the walking-route skill, and linked to the walks that start near where they end.

postTypes.name: Area and where-to-stay guides
postTypes.how: Neighbourhood guides and hotel guides. The hotel cards come from the Google Sheet through scripts/write-hotels.mjs and export-hotels.mjs, and hotel prices come from sampled booking pages, never from a single quoted night.

postTypes.name: Day trips
postTypes.how: Train facts checked against National Rail and the operators, with a dated GetYourGuide booking widget beside each recommended tour.

postTypes.name: Events and monthly guides
postTypes.how: Dated guides, such as Bonfire Night or London in October, that go out of date on their own. The weekly date check catches claims that have expired.

consensusSteps.detail: A topic file in data/topics/ holds the questions only Rob can answer, such as the price line or what counts. Collection waits until they are answered.

Start from what a reader would search. Take awards, magazines, independent blogs, video and real people's forum posts, and weigh a blogger or a Reddit thread as much as a magazine. Leave out booking sites, brand sites and content farms.

Each source goes into data/consensus/<topic>.json with the names it gives and what it said, checked against the known traps: one writer on four sites counts once, branches are kept apart, and closed places are dropped.
node scripts/build-evidence.mjs counts how many independent sources name each place and writes data/evidence.json.
The venue-check agent confirms each place is trading, and its address, against the venue's own site.

Short version first, then the evidence box, then entries. Every entry carries "Cited by N sources" and says what to order, what the room is like, and one thing that decides a visit. No weakness lines, and no notes about past mistakes.
A script per guide, scripts/verify-<topic>-citations.mjs, reads every figure back out of the article and fails if it no longer matches the evidence. npm run audit runs every health check.

Rob downloads three shots per place into scratchpad/downloaded-photos/<guide>/. A Sonnet agent picks the best of each and captions it from the guide's own text, then every photo is checked by eye against its caption. Heroes must be landscape.

Before a new guide is finished, it links to the guides a reader wants next, and every related guide, hub and planning page links back to it. For a hotel guide, that means the Where to stay page and the other stay guides. One inbound link is not enough, and node scripts/audit-links.mjs must pass.
Check the page on the local dev server and share the link.
Work is committed in the worktree and in main with the same message. Pushing to main deploys the site through Vercel, so it only happens when Rob says so.

siteFacts.label: Site
siteFacts.value: londontravelgeek.co.uk, built with Astro. Articles live in src/content/articles/.

siteFacts.label: Writing guide
siteFacts.value: CONTENT_GUIDELINES.md holds the rules every page follows. CLAUDE.md loads it into every Claude session and agent, and it is shown in full on this page.

siteFacts.label: Going live
siteFacts.value: A push to main on GitHub (RRM1000/london-travel-geek) makes Vercel build and deploy. A failed build leaves the previous version live.

siteFacts.label: Build checks
siteFacts.value: npm run build first checks image sizes and that every hero is landscape. The content schema rejects page titles over 55 characters.

siteFacts.label: Data
siteFacts.value: Restaurants, hotels and activities come from a Google Sheet through owner scripts. Consensus evidence lives in data/consensus/, data/topics/ and data/evidence.json. Analytics pulls land in data/analytics/latest.json.

siteFacts.label: Money
siteFacts.value: GetYourGuide (partner WWP7I0R), Hotels.com through CJ, and eSIM partners. The Affiliates section has the rules. Google Places, Apify and anything else billed needs a go-ahead before each run.

siteFacts.label: Firewall
siteFacts.value: The Vercel custom rule "Tencent scraper" challenges AS132203 (Tencent Cloud Singapore). It has been in place since 14 Sep 2026.

affiliates.lede: How the site earns: which programmes are live, where a booking link may go, and how the GetYourGuide widgets are placed and chosen. The counts are read from the articles each time this page is rebuilt.

items.name: Only where something is for sale
items.text: A link goes only where there's a ticket, tour or room to sell. A free park, a pub or a market gets none. Theatre, cinema, gigs and competitive socialising are booked direct with the venue.

items.name: The venue's own booking page wins
items.text: When the Sheet has a venue's booking link, no affiliate link is made for it. A booking page is a better landing than a reseller's search.

items.name: Labelled
items.text: Every affiliate link carries `rel="sponsored"` and a `data-affiliate` tag. Hotel and eSIM links in the text, and the booking cards, show a small "ad" chip.

items.name: Tours come early
items.text: On a tour or day trip guide, the Short Version says a reader can book a tour and what it saves them, and a tour section with a date widget follows the first practical section.

items.name: Placed by a script
items.text: `scripts/balance-gyg-widgets.mjs` places them and rewrites them on every run, so they're never added or moved by hand. It runs after `npm run build`, because it measures positions on the built page.

items.name: How many
items.text: By length: 1 under 1,500 words, 2 up to 3,500, 3 up to 6,000, and 4 above that.

items.name: Where
items.text: Never in the first quarter of the page, never two within 12% of each other (date widgets count), and always on the line before a heading. A page that can't meet both rules gets fewer widgets.

items.name: What each one shows
items.text: Set per guide in `data/gyg-queries.json`. Slot 1 is the page's subject. Slots 2 and 3 are big sellers, such as the Tower of London, the London Eye, a Windsor day trip or the London Pass, from a pool matched to the guide's area or category. Slot 4, on the longest pages, is the next thing that guide's reader would buy.

items.name: Choosing the search
items.text: Name a product, not a category: "Tower of London tickets", not "London top attractions". GetYourGuide's search never comes back empty, so a bad one quietly shows the wrong tours: the 4 Sep 2026 probe found 49 of 159 off the subject, some in other countries. Those slots show a hand-picked set of tours instead, such as `pick:harry-potter`, and the London Pass, Go City Explorer Pass and Merlin pass are pinned the same way as `pick:attraction-passes`, in every big-seller pool. Test a new search with `scripts/probe-gyg-queries.mjs`.

items.name: What they are
items.text: A booking calendar for one named tour, placed by hand beside the paragraph about that tour. The balancer never moves them.

items.name: Where they go
items.text: Guides where a bookable tour is the point, such as day trips and the Studio Tour. The guides that have one are listed below.

items.name: Choosing the tour
items.text: Compare the tours on GetYourGuide for what's included, rating, review count and price, and pick the one that does what the guide describes. The text links the same tour, tagged `cmp=<guide slug>`, so GetYourGuide's Campaigns report shows which guide sold it.

groups.title: Links in the text and sidebar

items.name: Tours named in the text
items.text: Link to the tour's own GetYourGuide page with `partner_id=WWP7I0R` and `cmp=<guide slug>`.

items.name: Things-to-do lists
items.text: Venues from the Activities sheet link to a checked product page in `data/gyg-tours.json` when there is one, and to a GetYourGuide search when not. A product page must be for the venue itself, an entry ticket or its own tour, never a coach trip that stops there.

items.name: Events
items.text: Link only when the Sheet's Affiliate URL is filled. GetYourGuide rarely sells exhibitions, and a generated search sent readers to unrelated tours.

items.name: Sidebar card
items.text: The pinned sidebar shows two bookable activities from the guide's own research. Guides with a Hotels.com page for their area show a hotel card instead: never both, because the column can't fit two.

items.name: Hotels.com through CJ
items.text: The one live hotel programme. The site's CJ id is PID 101875905. The theatre site has its own, and the CJ account number earns nothing.

items.name: How to link
items.text: `[name](hotel:slug)` for a hotel in the Hotels sheet: it earns once its Hotels.com URL column is filled, and links to the hotel's own site until then. `[name](hotelscom:<id>)` for a hotel the sheet doesn't hold. A hotel Hotels.com doesn't sell links to its own website, never another booking site.

items.name: Closed hotels
items.text: A hotel marked closed in `data/closed-hotels.json` loses its link in every guide.

items.name: Stay strips
items.text: A two-line Hotels.com search with check-in and check-out dates, one on guides under 2,500 words and two above, on things to do, areas, planning, transport and itinerary guides (not food or SIM pages). The balancer places them with the widgets, and may put them between the entries of a list. A light card with the same link sits under the tours card in the sidebar. Both open Hotels.com's London search through CJ, with the reader's dates when given.

items.name: Not switched on
items.text: Premier Inn, Travelodge, Hilton, IHG, Marriott, Accor and Hostelworld are set up in the code but stay off until you join the programme and add the ids.

items.name: eSIMs
items.text: Saily, Nomad (through Impact) and Klook, written as `[text](partner:saily-uk)`. The links live in `src/data/partnerLinks.json` and use the same accounts as Roam Compare.

items.name: Skiddle
items.text: Set up for event tickets, but off until `SKIDDLE_TAG` is added. A Skiddle link is the same Skiddle page with a tag on it, so it costs the reader nothing.

items.name: Clicks we can see
items.text: A click on any link tagged `data-affiliate` goes to Google Analytics as `affiliate_click`, with the network, the page section and the venue.

items.name: Clicks we can't
items.text: Clicks inside a GetYourGuide widget happen in GetYourGuide's own frame, so they show only in its partner dashboard.
